pages.text: Fire clay is clay that stands more heat. It is used for the things that get hottest: the crucible, fire bricks, fire ingot molds, channels and mold tables. There are few uses, and every one matters.
It is made of $(l:the_world/ores_and_minerals#graphite)Graphite$() powder ground in a $(l:crafting/quern)Quern$(), and $(l:the_world/ores_and_minerals#kaolinite)Kaolinite$() powder.
Kaolinite powder comes from heating $(l:the_world/ores_and_minerals#kaolinite)Kaolin Clay$() to 500 °C, but badly: only one piece in five becomes powder.
The unfired $(l:metalworking/crucible)Crucible$() is knapped from fire clay.
A $(l:metalworking/blast_furnace)Blast Furnace$() stack takes only fire bricks, reinforced with iron.
A $(thing)Fire Ingot Mold$() is the stronger $(l:getting_started/pottery#mold)Ingot Mold$(): it breaks once in 100 pours, a plain one once in 10.

Fire clay ware needs 1300 °C. That is hotter than a pit kiln gets (about 900 °C), and than coal reaches in a forge without bellows (950 °C on its own draught, 1228 °C with one person blowing, 1405 °C with two). Fire it in a $(l:metalworking/charcoal_forge)Charcoal Forge$() with a $(l:metalworking/bellows)Bellows$(). Ordinary clay ware needs only 850 °C.
